dedupe_keys.name: code and data repository for quantifying and partitioning uncertainty in multi scale urban water demand projections

description: Aniket Verma and colleagues publish a Python/R model for residential water-demand projections and uncertainty decomposition. Its documented Santa Cruz case combines climate, economic conditions, conservation, population growth, housing and household behaviour. Outputs span 2025–2050 at monthly and annual resolution, with city, block-group and household summaries. The September 2026 deposit provides code, example data and final statistics free under CC BY 4.0. The README describes execution scripts and recommends cluster processing for large scenario ensembles. Utility data-use restrictions remove the original DCC training database and fitted-result file; sensitive scenarios use public or synthetic substitutes, pipe diameters are zeroed, and rates use public 2021 values. Only samples of the full projection arrays are included. These limits matter when reproducing calibrated demand, not demonstrating the simulation workflow. No related catalogue record explicitly identifies the model. Exact installed dependency versions and execution success remain unknown; archives were not opened.
